top_signals.title: Johannesburg’s Infrastructure Decay Risks Driving Multinationals Out, Busi Mavuso Warns
top_signals.summary: Across Johannesburg, private companies are paving their own roads, trucking in water, and generating off-grid electricity just to stay operational. According to Busi Mavuso, CEO of Business Leadership South Africa, these compounding workaround costs are choking new investment and pushing more multinationals to reconsider their presence in the country. Speaking with Bloomberg’s Jennifer Zabasajja on Next Africa, Mavuso highlights how local manufacturing plants are steadily losing internal capital bids to overseas sister facilities, and why South Africa’s private sector can't afford to wait years for structural reforms to materialize. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Pandora Bets on Vietnam With New $150 Million Factory
top_signals.summary: Pandora has opened a new $150 million factory in Vietnam, its first production base outside Thailand. The expansion comes as the Danish jeweler tackles higher costs and tariff risks while growth in Asia helps offset weaker US demand. (Source: Bloomberg)
